articles.title: Future Value of a Lump Sum and an Annuity: One Formula, Two Cases
articles.excerpt: Future Value of a Lump Sum and an Annuity: One Formula, Two Cases "Future value" shows up anywhere you project money forward: a one-time deposit, a monthly savings plan, a pension contribution schedul…
articles.body: Future Value of a Lump Sum and an Annuity: One Formula, Two Cases "Future value" shows up anywhere you project money forward: a one-time deposit, a monthly savings plan, a pension contribution schedule. Developers often reach for a loop, but the two canonical cases have closed forms. Get those right and you can handle most projections without iterating year by year. Case 1: a single lump sum A single amount PV invested at rate r per period for n periods: FV = PV * (1 + r)^n This is compound interest with the periods already normalized — r is the per-period rate, so if your input is an annual nominal rate compounded monthly, use r/12 and n = years * 12 .

articles.body: You have connected Contact Form 7 to Monday.com through a connector plugin. The API logs show a successful 200 OK response. The item ID is returned. Everything looks correct. But when you open the board in Monday.com, the item is not there. This is one of the most confusing integration failures because the API tells you it succeeded. The request was valid. The item was created. But it is invisible to you. This guide explains exactly why this happens and how to fix it. Why Monday.com Says "Success" When the Item Is Invisible Monday.com's API creates items at the account level, not at the board level. The create_item mutation accepts a board_id and returns the created item's ID and URL.

articles.body: Invoice PDFs that sometimes never finished rendering. That was the bug. It took far longer to find than to fix, and the cause was strange enough that I want to write it down. The setup I'm building Freveo , a workspace for freelancers: proposals, invoices, change orders, time tracking. Every invoice, contract and timesheet is rendered to PDF in headless Chromium, in a separate PDF service. The API runs on Bun. The symptom Renders sometimes never finished. I first saw it in CI, once the new change-order tests started running beside the invoice tests. Nothing failed with an error. A render just sat there until the test runner gave up. Locally it was hard to trigger, which is the worst kind of bug to have. The wrong fix My first move was a longer test timeout.

articles.title: SCIM filters are query syntax, not an authorization policy
articles.excerpt: SCIM filters are query syntax, not an authorization policy Identity synchronization often depends on a filter such as userName sw "contractor" or a group filter in a provisioning connector. Teams use…
articles.body: SCIM filters are query syntax, not an authorization policy Identity synchronization often depends on a filter such as userName sw "contractor" or a group filter in a provisioning connector. Teams use those expressions to decide which accounts belong in an application. A malformed or overbroad filter can therefore create a security-relevant population change. The filter grammar is precise, but the business rule around it needs separate review. RFC 7644 defines SCIM filtering as an optional protocol feature. A service provider may decline to filter results when it does not recognize a requested operation. The specification requires valid expressions and defines operators such as equality, presence, starts with, ends with, contains, and comparison operators for supported attributes.

articles.excerpt: If you’ve ever written complex WebGL shaders or procedural raymarching scenes, you already know the pain of raw GLSL: everything has to live in one giant, monolithic file. Unlike C, C++, or modern web…
articles.body: If you’ve ever written complex WebGL shaders or procedural raymarching scenes, you already know the pain of raw GLSL: everything has to live in one giant, monolithic file. Want to reuse your favorite math utilities, signed distance field (SDF) shapes, or lighting helpers across different projects? Good luck copying and pasting code blocks across files, or wrestling with hacky string-injection scripts in your build setup. That frustration led me to build glslh—a lightweight, C-style #include preprocessor and live VS Code extension designed to bring true modularity to shader development. I recently hit 570+ installs in its first week, so I wanted to share the architecture behind it and how it solves the modularity problem for WebGL developers.

articles.body: SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force from California tonight (Nov. 11), the second such flight for the company in a six-day span. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from California's Vandenberg Space Force Base tonight at 11:36 p.m. EST (8:36 p.m. local California time; 0136 GMT on Nov. 12), kicking off a mission called USSF-627. Vandenberg hosted a similar liftoff less than a week ago: On Nov. 6, a Falcon 9 sent the USSF-432 mission skyward from the site, which lies on California's gorgeous but often foggy central coast. A Falcon 9 first stage rests on a SpaceX drone ship shortly after launching the USSF-627 mission on Nov. 11, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) We don't know much about USSF-627 or USSF-432; both are classified.

articles.excerpt: Fast radio bursts are invisible, but a composer has turned thousands of them into sound at a Finnish cathedral, where a choir will sing along on Nov. 21.
articles.body: Fast radio bursts, flashes of energy from faraway galaxies, are invisible to our eyes. However, we can now hear their melody, thanks to a composer who has turned them into sound. Fast radio bursts, or FRBs , are among the most extreme events in the universe, releasing as much energy in a millisecond as the sun puts out in three days and briefly outshining entire galaxies. Since the first FRB was discovered in 2007, astronomers have detected thousands of them; however, exactly how these cosmic flares are launched remains poorly understood. Recent evidence points to at least one burst coming from the environment around a rotating neutron star. Despite their power, FRBs last only a few thousandths of a second before vanishing into space.

articles.title: OpenAI is sunsetting ChatGPT Advanced and Standard voice next month
articles.excerpt: OpenAI is going all in on GPT-Live.
articles.body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR OpenAI has announced that it will retire ChatGPT Advanced and Standard voice on December 11, 2026. The company is focusing on unifying the voice experience through GPT-Live. Live video and screen sharing will continue to use Advanced voice until GPT-Live has this capability. Earlier this year, OpenAI rolled out a new voice model called GPT-Live . The Gemini Live rival joined ChatGPT Advanced and Standard voice as yet another way to have more natural conversations with the chatbot. As the saying goes, three is a crowd, and OpenAI is ready to do some streamlining. OpenAI has announced that a big change is coming for ChatGPT Voice. On December 11, 2026, the company will be retiring Advanced and Standard voice.
